pr.title: Remove a delivered worktree and branch without asking again during cleanup
pr.head: 5d9b64bce626833d42bbba3686e9cb88cf4e9e4c

summary: The cleanup skill ends an agent session. It checks that the session finished its work, asks the user what to do with anything left, and then releases what the session holds, including the Git worktrees and local branches it created.

Before this change, two Git safety checks made the skill stop and ask the user about worktrees and branches whose work had already merged. Claude Code's ExitWorktree tool compares a worktree with the local copy of the branch it started from, so a stale local main made merged commits look unmerged. git branch -d refuses a squash-merged branch once its remote branch is deleted, because the squash put different commits on main.

The skill already proves delivery itself, in step 4 of "Take stock of the session": every commit is on a remote, or sits at or below the head of the merged pull request. This change makes the release steps rely on that proof, and the user's request to clean up counts as consent. Step 4 runs before the skill stops the session's subagents, so the skill runs its checks again on each worktree and branch just before it removes it. When the checks pass, the skill passes ExitWorktree's discard_changes: true after a stale-branch refusal and deletes branches with git branch -D, both without asking. A change that exists nowhere else is still a gap that the user answers, and the skill discards it only when the user says to.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Gap: work the session owes and has not delivered, such as a commit that exists only in a local worktree. The skill asks the user about each gap.
  • Step 4: the delivery check in "Take stock of the session". It runs git status --porcelain and git log HEAD --not --remotes in each worktree, and for a squash-merged branch it looks up the merged pull request's headRefOid and counts each commit after it as undelivered.
  • Override: a host tool's flag that removes a worktree despite its own safety check, such as ExitWorktree's discard_changes: true.

cards.title: What the review checked
cards.html:
• In a sandbox with a bare remote and a stubbed gh, step 4 reported a gap for a commit after the merged head, an untracked file, a staged change, a detached HEAD with an unpushed commit, and a reused branch name.
  • Earlier reviews found that step 4's result goes stale once subagents stop, first for the worktree override and then for git branch -D. This head reruns the checks before every removal, and the review of it is clean.

groups.title: Release steps rely on the delivery check
groups.kicker: Worktrees and branches that step 4 cleared go without a second question
intro: The release section removes what the session holds in a fixed order: subscriptions, subagents and background work, reviews, inbox items, worktrees, branches, and stashes. This group changes the worktree and branch steps.

1. Re-check. Just before it removes each worktree or branch, the skill runs step 4's checks again, because a subagent can commit or leave edits after step 4 and before release step 2 stops it. A change the re-check finds becomes a gap that the user answers.
  2. Worktrees. The skill removes each worktree the re-check clears, without asking. When a host tool refuses because a stale local branch lacks the worktree's commits, it passes the tool's override. A refusal that names an uncommitted file makes the worktree a gap.
  3. Branches. The skill deletes a cleared branch with git branch -D, because git branch -d refuses a squash-merged branch whose remote branch is gone. It still keeps the branch of an open pull request.
docs/plugins.md describes the same behavior for readers of the plugin documentation.

checks.text: Both steps still apply only to worktrees and branches the session created. The skill's opening section forbids touching the user's checkout or another session's worktree, and this change leaves that rule as it was.

files.note: A new paragraph makes release steps 5 (worktrees) and 6 (branches) rerun step 4's checks just before each removal, and both steps then act on that re-check without asking.

checks.text: In a sandbox, a branch that was clean at step 4 got an unpushed commit before release step 2. Rerunning step 4 reported it as a gap before git worktree remove and again before git branch -D. A worktree that got an untracked file after step 4 was also reported.
On a squash-merged branch whose remote branch is deleted, git branch -d printed not fully merged in a sandbox, and git branch -D deleted it.

files.note: Says that cleanup removes a worktree or branch without asking once every commit on it is on a remote or in a merged pull request.
